Yemen’s Presidential Leadership Council chairman Rashad al-Alimi promised a firm response. ... Putin reportedly proposed talks alongside next month’s APEC summit in China to discuss ending the war. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed discussions about a meeting but said neither its format nor agenda was settled. ... The World Food Programme has cut monthly food assistance in Gaza from 1.6 million people to 1.1 million after its funding fell to less than half previous levels. Families now receive one food parcel instead of two, cash payments have been reduced, and daily hot meals have fallen from 250,000 to 150,000. The agency warns that recent improvements in food security could quickly reverse. ... Around 1.4 million people, or 67% of Gaza’s population, still face crisis-level hunger or worse, including 200,000 in emergency conditions. More than 80% of residents are unemployed, leaving many unable to buy food even when it is available. ... World Food Programme Palestine director Shaun Hughes said recovery investment was essential because the humanitarian operation was unsustainable. Reconstruction promised after the October 2025 ceasefire has not begun. The agency needs $450 million to maintain critical operations across Gaza and the West Bank through March. Japan launched its Martian Moons Exploration spacecraft aboard an H3 rocket on Tuesday, beginning a five-year mission to collect samples from Phobos, the larger of Mars’ two moons. The spacecraft separated successfully after launch from Tanegashima Island. No mission has previously returned material from Mars or either moon, and earlier attempts to reach Phobos have failed. ... The spacecraft is expected to reach Mars next year. A French-German rover named Idefix will survey Phobos for 100 days before a Japanese lander attempts to collect at least 10 grams of material in late 2028 or 2029. The samples are scheduled to return to Earth in Australia in 2031. ... items.title: Fed sees AI boom adding to inflation headache, but others may pay for the medicine By Reuters
items.excerpt: CLEVELAND, Oct 19 (Reuters) - The artificial intelligence boom, increasingly acknowledged at the Federal Reserve as helping drive inflation, has left central bankers faced with cooling the rest of the economy to lower price pressures amplified by an industry of marquee names like Amazon, Apple and Anthropic considered immune to rate hikes. ... Fed officials know their blunt tool of raising borrowing costs lands unevenly. With AI firms spending as if money is no object, economists see the pain of rate hikes falling elsewhere, on firms and families more reliant on credit, or small- and medium-sized businesses that temper their investment plans as borrowing costs escalate. ... "There are paths to get there," ADP Chief Economist Nela Richardson said of the Fed’s 2% inflation goal, unmet for more than five years. "It’s just not every road is open," with the housing market already weak, for example, and the labor market not seen as a source of inflation through rising wages. ... The Fed meets October 27-28 and is expected to keep rates steady at 3.75%-4.00%. Fed officials say further hikes are likely needed and are now debating the pace and extent.

Shares in SpaceX spiked 3% in post-market trading after the release of third-quarter results. ... • Today’s Key Market Moves STOCKS: Asia in the red: South Korea -3.5%, Japan -1.5%. Europe slips, France lags. Americas in the green: Brazil +1.5%, Dow +1%, S&P 500 +0.3%, Nasdaq flat, small-cap Russell 2000 index +1.7%, biggest rise since August 4.SECTORS/SHARES: Nine sectors on the S&P 500 rise, two fall. Healthcare +2.3%, comms services -0.9%. Biggest gainers on S&P 500 Equifax, Hasbro +11%; biggest decliner General Motors -7%. Netflix -6% after the bell.FX: Dollar down broadly. Biggest G10 climbers are sterling to five-week high, Canadian dollar to one-month high. Colombian peso biggest decliner.BONDS: Japanese yields slide, French yields dip but spread over bunds has widest close since 2011. French CDS highest since 2013. US yields -5 bps at long end, +2 bps at short end.COMMODITIES/METALS: Oil hits six-month high, then closes lower: Brent -0.7%, WTI -1.8%. ... Markets and economies around the world are taking the global energy shock in their stride, but if that’s because they’re expecting prices to fall any time soon, they may have to readjust. Oil prices closed lower on Tuesday, but not before Brent and WTI crude futures clocked fresh six-month peaks — Brent nudged $112/barrel and WTI rose above $110. It seems a lifetime ago, but when the US and Iran signed the MOU in June, an end to the war, opening of the Strait of Hormuz, and replenishing of global energy supplies seemed imminent. WTI’s year-on-year price change even briefly turned negative. But now, WTI is nearly 80% more expensive than it was a year ago and inflationary pressures, although supply-driven, are increasingly difficult for policymakers to look through. Will today’s reported Iran-Pakistan talks open the door to a US-Iran detente?

items.title: Wall Street gains as healthcare stocks rally, oil prices fall By Reuters
items.excerpt: Oct 20 (Reuters) - The Dow rose 1% on Tuesday, outperforming the benchmark S&P 500 while the healthcare sector provided Wall Street’s biggest boost and technology was its biggest drag. Healthcare led gains among the S&P 500’s 11 major sector indexes, hitting a record high. Eli Lilly was the S&P 500’s biggest index point contributor while UnitedHealth, Merck & Co, Johnson & Johnson and Amgen helped boost the blue-chip Dow industrials. Declines in megacap stocks pulled down the communication services sector. Energy shares underperformed as oil prices fell after touching a five-month high. Oil traders were weighing a meeting between the Iranian president and Pakistan’s army chief, a US-Iran mediator, against Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf. ... The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 529.85 points, or 1.02%, to 52,495.88, the S&P 500 gained 21.84 points, or 0.28%, to 7,712.57 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 6.07 points, or 0.02%, to 26,424.82. The S&P 500 value index rose 0.9% compared with a 0.2% drop in its growth counterpart. The small-cap Russell 2000 index finished up 1.7%. ... SpaceX reported a third-quarter profit after the market closed that blew past estimates, boosting its shares 4% in late trading. ... General Motors shares sank 6.8% after the automaker signaled pressure in coming months from higher commodity costs and lower truck sales. 3M rose 5.8% after the company said it was expanding its data-center partnership with Amazon and issued a warrant to an Amazon subsidiary to purchase 3M common stock worth over $521 million. The industrial conglomerate also raised its full-year profit forecast. ... Credit reporting firm Equifax rallied 11.3% after it reported third-quarter profit above analysts’ estimates. Hasbro shares jumped 11.2% after the toymaker raised its full-year forecast for both overall revenue and its digital gaming business.

Airline fares rose significantly, while hotel and motel room prices and portfolio management fees fell, impacting the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Indexes, which the Federal Reserve tracks for its 2% inflation target. items.excerpt: President Trump and Vice President Vance on Tuesday announced in the Oval Office the establishment of a whistleblower “incentive program” aimed to uncover fraud. “Every day, President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud is zeroing in on the rampant abuse of taxpayer dollars and giving Americans the accountability they deserve. This administration has zero tolerance for individuals who steal from Americans,” White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said. Trump’s envoys held meetings Tuesday in Norway with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, along with the leaders of Norway and Finland, the Norwegian government said, as Trump pushes for an end to Russia and Ukraine’s nearly five-year conflict. Trump on Monday told reporters, “All I want for Russia and Ukraine is for them to stop the stupid war.” Steve Witkoff will meet with Zelensky and others in person, with Jared Kushner meeting virtually. With just two weeks before November’s midterms, Trump will continue his GOP midterm tour later in the day, travelling to Greenville, N.C., for a rally. He is expected to make a case for Republican National Committee Chair Michael Whatley, but polls place his Democratic opponent Gov. Roy Cooper firmly in the lead. The president also hosted a rally last month in Gastonia, N.C. ## North Carolina mail-in ballot restrictions to remain through midterms, judge rules A federal judge ruled Monday that North Carolina is permitted to keep its strict mail-in ballot rules in place for November’s election, which were changed just before ballots were mailed in September. In the ruling, Judge Thomas D. Shroeder wrote that it was too close to the election to change the rules again, and that plaintiffs waited too long to file their motion. Read more here. ## Musk endorses Paxton in Texas Senate race Tech mogul Elon Musk has formally endorsed Republican Ken Paxton in the Texas Senate race after bankrolling his campaign for several weeks. The tech billionaire and one-time trillionaire has spent more than $150 million on Paxton’s candidacy as the lone donor to Texas PAC, a political action committee supporting Paxton. In a post to the social platform X — which Musk owns — Tuesday, Musk encouraged Texans to get out and support the Texas Attorney General. Read more here. ... ## Sabato's Crystal Ball moves nearly 3 dozen House races in Democrats favor Nonpartisan election forecaster Sabato’s Crystal Ball is moving 28 House races in Democrats’ direction with just two weeks until the midterms. When adding up the seats Crystal Ball says are either safe, likely or leaning toward one party, the new projections put Democrats above the 218 needed for a House majority. In other words, Democrats could lose every race rated as “toss-up” and still win if Crystal Ball’s ratings prove accurate. ... ## 7 in 10 doubt Trump would accept GOP losses in midterms: Survey A new poll shows that most Americans surveyed doubt President Trump will accept the midterm election results if Republicans sustain losses in Congress and lose their majority. The Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll found that 70 percent of respondents are not confident Trump will accept the results, including 36 percent of Republicans, 77 percent of independents and 94 percent of Democrats. There’s confidence among 28 percent of respondents that Trump will accept the midterm results. Sixty-three percent of Republicans are confident Trump will accept the results, as are 21 percent of independents, while 6 percent of Democrats are confident he will accept the results.

items.excerpt: Entertainment News (10/21/26) - BusinessWorld Online # Entertainment News (10/21/26) PRODUCER, songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist Ziv has teamed up with rising P-pop girl group VVINK for “Trisikulo,” a pop track on the familiar third-wheel experience. October 20, 2026 | 6:06 pm ## Ziv, VVINK release collaboration PRODUCER, songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist Ziv has teamed up with rising P-pop girl group VVINK for “Trisikulo,” a pop track on the familiar third-wheel experience. Released under Sony Music Entertainment, it is built around Filipino wordplay that links a tricycle’s three wheels to the feeling of being the extra person in someone else’s love story. The song was co-written by Ziv alongside Paolo Benjamin Guico of Filipino folk-pop band Ben&Ben and Angelika Samantha Ortiz, one of the songwriters behind BINI’s hit “Pantropiko.” The mixing was also done by Jacques Jenkins and mastering by Luna Tebbs. The track is out now on all digital music streaming platforms. ## *Love in Disguise* premieres on Prime Video *LOVE in Disguise*, a Korean series based on the hit web novel *Why Don’t You Know It’s a Girl?*, has premiered on Prime Video. It is directed by Park Dhan-hee and stars Yim Si Wan, Seorina, Kim Junghyun, and Yeonwoo. The genre-blending romance is exclusively seen on Prime Video in the Philippines and in more than 240 countries and territories worldwide. ## Estelle Fly drops club-pop single SINGAPOREAN pop artist Estelle Fly has released “Shut It Down,” a playful club-pop single about switching off the overthinking and making the dance floor your own. Inspired by the Rihanna and Kesha songs, the new release is an invitation to let loose, dance with friends and have fun even when life feels complicated. It is out now on all digital music streaming platforms. ## Cayabyab, APO, Mitch Valdes reunion THIS holiday season, National Artist for Music Ryan Cayabyab, OPM legends APO, and performer Mitch Valdes will come together for *naRyan nAPO Kami*, the fourth chapter of the MaestroClass Concert Series. The shows will be held on Dec. 4, 5, and 6 at the Proscenium Theater at Rockwell Center, Makati. All shows take place at 7:30 p.m. Joined by the Ryan Cayabyab Singers, the special Christmas chapter of the concert series brings together familiar songs, stories, and artists in a celebration that captures the warmth and spirit of a Filipino family gathering. Tickets are available directly at the Proscenium Theater website via *https://prosceniumtheater.com/* and at the Power Plant Mall Cinema. ## *Amir* gets international distribution GMA Pictures, GMA Public Affairs, and Brightburn Entertainment have officially locked in a partnership deal with Columbia Pictures for the distribution of the upcoming fantasy-drama film and 52 nd Metro Manila Film Festival (MMFF) finalist *Amir*. It is directed by Zig Dulay, with a script crafted by National Artist for Film and Broadcast Arts Ricky Lee alongside Anj Atienza. The film’s cast features Dennis Trillo, Argus Aspiras, Glaiza de Castro, Will Ashley, Caprice Cayetano, Epy Quizon, Joel Saracho, Ronnie Lazaro, Laila Ulao, Heath Jornales, Yasser Marta, Mad Ramos, Ethan Hariot, Hebron Ecal, and Mon Confiado. ## Rachel Chinouriri releases new album UK’s indie-pop singer-songwriter Rachel Chinouriri has released her second studio album, I think I spoke too soon, via Atlas Artists/Parlophone Records. The album expands upon the pop, indie, and rock influences that Ms. Chinouriri has long used to sketch portraits of her inner world. The album’s focus track is “Pretty girls,” which celebrates women, self-confidence, and the freedom to express oneself without fear of judgement. ## M2M 2027 world tour has Manila leg NORWEGIAN pop duo M2M have announced that their global tour *TWO* will be coming to Manila in 2027. The tour will start in March and after concerts at Mexico, Singapore, Hong Kong, and Jakarta, M2M’s global tour will reach Manila on April 2, 2027, at the Araneta Coliseum in Quezon City. Tickets will go on sale on Oct. 24 at 10 a.m. via *TicketNet.com.ph* and TicketNet outlets nationwide. Presented by Wilbros Live, the concert will feature M2M performing their greatest hits, “Don’t Say You Love Me,” “Mirror Mirror,” “Pretty Boy,” and “The Day You Went Away,” among others. ## Maris Racal appears in Maya Black’s music video ACTRESS Maris Racal is featured in Maya Black’s latest music video, serving edgy looks against a hyperpop track. In the video, everything she wants turns into a miniature version of itself, bringing the song’s “make it mini” message to life. The idea behind it is all about having more flexibility when it comes to bigger purchases, to promote Maya’s Mini Payments offering. The music video starring Maris Racal can be viewed here: *https://youtu.be/b\_zKjZ6u2f4?si=q8AzbC9iUSLp0sAV*. With Mini Payments, eligible purchases made using the Maya Black credit card can be converted into three, six, nine, or 12 monthly payments.
